title: Test recognition rejects a quoted '|' inside one argument as a compound command (node --test-name-pattern regex)
outcome: A correctly quoted single focused command containing '|' inside one argument is recognized and credited by its result
acceptance: A focused command whose only '|' characters are inside a single- or double-quoted argument is recognized as one command and judged on its result when it is an unwrapped command (no bash -c, pwsh -Command or cmd /c wrapper) whose shell dialect is known to the host (today: commands from Claude's Bash tool, POSIX quoting); a command of unknown dialect, and every wrapper form containing a quoted '|', stays ineligible (UNKNOWN) with a truthful reason; an unquoted '|' is still rejected as compound.
Regression tests cover a quoted regex alternation in a node --test-name-pattern argument, an unquoted pipeline, and mixed quoting, through the same recognizer the host uses for credit.
Focused tests and the full gate pass on the final input, and independent reviews find no unresolved in-scope Medium or higher.
